newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uraltelekom 1996 net rises over 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uraltelekom 1996 net rises over 50 pct.

text.p: NOTES -- Figures are calculated to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis.

Shareholders of telecoms company AO Uraltelekom, based in the Urals region of Russia, approved at their annual meeting on Tuesday an increase in authorised capital to 541.19 billion roubles from 96.64 billion roubles through a revaluation of assets.
The nominal value of company shares would rise to 84,000 roubles from 15,000 roubles after the capital increase.
"It is necessary to bring Uraltelekom's charter capital into line with company assets," Deputy General Director for economy Galina Ptichenko said at the meeting.
"The increase in capital will also boost the reputation of the company and increase the liquidity of the shares."

But state telecoms holding company AO Svyazinvest, which has a controlling 50.7 percent stake of voting shares, did not approve a new share issue since it did not have funds to buy new shares, Ptichenko said.
Shareholders approved international accountants Price Waterhouse as the company's auditors.
Individuals own 38 percent of shares, Taft Enterprises Ltd owns 11.3 percent, CS First Boston owns seven percent and AO Sredneuralskoye owns four percent.
Dividend payments on preferred shares will start on August 1, on ordinary shares held by individuals, on September 1 and on ordinaries held by legal entities, on December 1.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
